editorial_intro: Spider-Man just dethroned The Force Awakens — $944.5M domestic, the all-time North American record — while Resident Evil took the weekend with a $60M franchise-best opening. In Indian cinema, the weekend's real story is survival: Mandaadi crossed ₹100 Cr worldwide and flattened Sardar 2, Hanuman Ansh hit ₹272 Cr India on 151x its ₹2 Cr budget, and Mirzapur: The Movie is now Pankaj Tripathi's most profitable film ever. Bollywood's Friday newcomers struggled — Vibe's ₹7.45 Cr opening beat Daayra's ₹5.63 Cr, but neither found the audience it needed — and all eyes are on Sept 24, when Nani's The Paradise arrives with record US advance sales.

movies.title: Resident Evil
movies.why_watch: The horror event of the fall delivered: a $60M domestic opening — the best in franchise history — on a $108.3M global launch. Zach Cregger (Barbarian, Weapons) ditched the lore for a lean 90-minute single-night survival ride through Raccoon City, and at 96% RT it's officially the highest-rated video game adaptation ever made. Horror cinema's I.P. era finally has a benchmark.

movies.title: Bad Apples
movies.why_watch: Saoirse Ronan is having the most fun of her career playing the worst version of herself — a primary-school teacher who locks a feral 10-year-old in her basement and accidentally becomes the best educator in England. 83% on Rotten Tomatoes and genuinely, uncomfortably funny: the rare dark comedy that gets darker every fifteen minutes and keeps earning it.

movies.title: Daayra
movies.why_watch: The week's prestige pick arrived to a box-office thud: just ₹5.63 Cr nett over the opening weekend, with a Monday hold now deciding its fate. But don't confuse business with quality — Meghna Gulzar's crime thriller passed the CBFC with zero visual cuts, and the Kareena Kapoor/Prithviraj Sukumaran cop-versus-cop collision is exactly the serious Hindi cinema theaters keep asking for. Catch it before the BOGO offers end.

movies.title: Vibe
movies.why_watch: The family clash's funnier half won round one: ₹7.45 Cr over opening weekend, clearly ahead of sister-in-law Kareena's Daayra. Kunal Kemmu writes, directs and stars as one of two hopelessly unqualified best friends roped into a terror plot, and Preity Zinta's return as the mysterious Madam H is the comeback story Bollywood loves. Madgaon Express was 2024's sharpest comedy — if Vibe holds half that chaos, it's the crowd-pleaser of the month.

movies.title: Mirzapur: The Movie
movies.why_watch: The OTT-to-theater leap that actually worked: ₹216 Cr India in 17 days, a steady ₹12.25 Cr third weekend, and now officially Pankaj Tripathi's most profitable film ever — bigger than OMG 2. Kaleen Bhaiya on the big screen turned out to be an event, not a cash-grab. Week three, still running strong.

movies.title: Hanuman Ansh
movies.why_watch: The box-office miracle of the year refuses to leave: ₹271.88 Cr India in 45 days — a ₹2 Cr devotional now running at 151x its budget and the third-highest Hindi grosser of 2026. It even out-grossed Daayra and Vibe in its SEVENTH weekend (₹28.5 Cr). Neem Karoli Baba's story is the kind of theatrical phenomenon money can't buy. Still running, sequel confirmed.

movies.title: Mandaadi
movies.why_watch: The Tamil duel is officially a rout: Soori's sailboat-racing drama crossed ₹100 Cr worldwide on day 11 (₹103.72 Cr), with a second Sunday of ₹8 Cr growing 22% week-on-week — while Sardar 2 limped to ₹23.35 Cr. Soori's biggest hit as a solo lead by miles, and the interval and climax boat-race sequences remain the ones everyone's talking about. The Tamil pick of the month, full stop.

movies.title: Bethlehem Kudumba Unit
movies.why_watch: The highest-grossing Malayalam film of ALL TIME — ₹157.45 Cr worldwide — is still pulling crowds in limited US shows in its fifth weekend. Nivin Pauly's age-gap rom-com from the Premalu director turned out to be the crossover comedy that cracked every market. Diaspora audiences, this is your victory lap: the biggest Malayalam hit ever, still in theaters near you.

movies.title: Practical Magic 2
movies.why_watch: The witches are in trouble: down 59% in weekend two with just $12.2M, for a $76.8M global total on a $75M budget. Bullock and Kidman remain the draw and 1998 nostalgia runs deep — but the movie now needs genuine legs against Resident Evil to justify its budget. One for the faithful, in theaters while the coven lasts.

movies.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
movies.why_watch: It's official: $944.5M domestic, and Spider-Man: Brand New Day is now the highest-grossing film in the history of the North American box office — dethroning The Force Awakens after 11 years. Add $2.4B worldwide (#3 all-time) and the question is no longer whether it's a hit, but whether anything in theaters can touch it. Catch the record-holder on the big screen.

movies.title: Coyote vs. Acme
movies.why_watch: The rescue story of the year keeps paying off: $4.5M this weekend puts the shelved-tax-writeoff turned theatrical darling past $52M domestic. 96% RT, an A CinemaScore, and the best Looney Tunes movie ever made. John Cena vs. Wile E. Coyote in court — still the feel-good family watch of the season.

movies.title: The Paradise
movies.why_watch: This week's must-watch list starts Thursday: Nani and Dasara director Srikanth Odela's big-budget Telugu action epic already smashed records in US advance sales — $100K in four hours through Cinemark alone, the fastest Telugu film ever to do it. Trade is projecting $1.5-2M from overseas premieres. Book your seats early; this one is tracking like a tsunami.
